//: Copy agent-queue.config.example.json to agent-queue.config.json (gitignored) and fill it in, or point AGENT_QUEUE_CONFIG at another file. Keys ending in Note, and every "//" key, are documentation and are ignored on load.

human.name: Alex
human.nameNote: The person the queue works for. Prompts, worker briefs, ticket comments and Slack lines use it ("ask Alex").

orchestrator.sessionNameNote: The pinned Claude Code session that writes specs and watches the queue. Emergency responders message it by this name.
orchestrator.lockFileNote: The driver lock: the session ID of the one session allowed to approve and merge. merge-approved.sh refuses any other Claude Code session, and reads the lock again right before each merge. A shell outside Claude Code counts as the human and passes. null means <paths.sharedDir>/orchestrator-session, so a takeover on one machine stops the driver on every other. The lease sits beside it.
orchestrator.approvalsFileNote: The approvals ledger merge-approved.sh writes: one JSON line per approved PR head, closed by a merged line. An approval covers only the exact head it names. null means <paths.sharedDir>/approvals.jsonl, so a session on another machine sees the same approvals.
orchestrator.leaseMinutesNote: The lease is the driver's heartbeat, renewed when it takes over, ends a turn, runs a merge or its watcher fires. Older than this, the supervisor counts the driver as idle. It never stops the driver from acting.
orchestrator.handoffFileNote: The note the orchestrator keeps of what is in flight, which takeover.sh prints for the next driver. null means <paths.sharedDir>/ORCHESTRATOR.md.
orchestrator.eventsDirNote: Where dispatchers leave notices for the orchestrator, one JSON file each ({id, host, subtitle, text, link, at}), which dispatcher-events-watch.mjs reports. null means <paths.sharedDir>/orchestrator-events.
orchestrator.supervisorNote: orchestrator-supervisor.mjs, installed by inbox/install-supervisor.sh on the orchestrator's machine, runs every everyMinutes. When the lease has expired and work has waited waitMinutes on the orchestrator, it pages slack.channel: once, then again at each of repageMinutes after the first page, then not again until a driver renews the lease. A page Slack refuses is retried after 5 minutes, doubling to an hour. It never starts a session or moves the lock. Touch <paths.stateDir>/supervisor.off to silence it.
orchestrator.prSweepNote: pr-sweep.mjs reports open PRs every everyHours: approved at their current head but idle approvedIdleHours, with no owner, or owned with nothing moving for staleHours. A claim (pr-sweep.mjs own) lasts ownerTtlHours. PRs by reportOnlyAuthors (gh logins) are listed apart. ignoreActivityChecks are regex sources for checks a workflow re-sets on every PR, which are not activity.

repoPathNote: The local main checkout of the repo the queue builds. Workers cut their worktrees from it, and the pre-merge check keeps its scratch worktree under it.
workspaceCwdNote: The folder workers start in (fleet.sh dispatch --cwd). Usually the repo's parent, so a worker can see sibling repos.
worktreesDirNote: Where worktrees live, relative to repoPath.

paths.stateDirNote: Per machine: state.json, logs, the PAUSED flag, the tick lock, and the secret files (slack-webhook, slack-bot-token, linear-api-key).
paths.sharedDirNote: Shared across machines: merge-requests/, heartbeats/, bundles/, wake-requests/, orchestrator-events/ and main-state.json. With more than one machine, point it at a folder Syncthing or Dropbox keeps in sync.

github.repoNote: owner/name of the repo the queue builds.
github.userNote: The gh account the dispatcher and merge scripts act as (gh auth token --user).
github.baseBranchNote: The branch PRs target and the main watcher reads.
github.ciWorkflowNote: The workflow name the pre-merge check and the main watcher read.
github.reviewCheckNote: The status check that must pass before a PR counts as green. null skips the review check.
github.rerunLabelNote: merge-when-ready.sh adds this label once when the review check reads "Re-review not requested". null if your review bot re-runs on every push.
github.fixesMainLabelNote: A PR with this label may merge while main is red or the merge queue is held.
github.fixTitlePrefixNote: Optional title prefix that also marks a PR as a fix for merge-approved.sh, e.g. "Revert \"" for GitHub's revert PRs. null means only the label counts.
github.branchTemplateNote: The branch a worker builds on. {id} is the lowercased ticket ID, so ENG-123 builds on agent/eng-123.

linear.teamNote: The team key. It is also the ticket prefix (ENG-123).
linear.apiKeyCommandNote: Optional argv that prints the Linear API key, for a secrets manager, e.g. ["doppler", "secrets", "get", "LINEAR_API_KEY", "--plain"]. The LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable wins over it. With neither, the key is read from apiKeyFile.
linear.apiKeyFileNote: The file holding the Linear API key when neither the environment nor apiKeyCommand gives one. Mode 600.
linear.inboxProjectNote: The Linear project ask-human.sh files an ask into when it is not about a ticket.
linear.sizeLabelGroupNote: The Linear label group whose child labels (S, M, L) size a ticket.

labels.labelsNote: ready, building and stuck are the queue's states. needsHuman marks a ticket with an open ask. sentry, mechanical and judgment drive the Sentry lane; leave them as they are if you have no Sentry triage.

states.statesNote: Workflow state names on the team. A claimed ticket moves to inProgress, a merged one to verifying.

linear.verifyEvidenceHeadingNote: The heading a verify evidence comment opens with (docs/ticket-spec.md). merged-to-verifying.mjs leaves a ticket in Done only when its newest evidence comment by an accepted author came after the merge and passes: the footer, at least one PASS row, and no FAIL or malformed row.
linear.verifyEnvironmentsNote: The environment names an evidence footer may name (_Verified <ISO> on <env> as <persona> against <sha>_).
linear.verifyEvidenceAuthorsNote: Linear user IDs whose evidence comments count, besides the user the Linear API key belongs to. A comment by anyone else is ignored.

slack.domainNote: The subdomain in https://<domain>.slack.com, used to build thread links.
slack.channelNote: The channel ID asks and progress lines go to. Keep it private: it carries ticket titles.
slack.channelNameNote: The channel's display name, used in docs and prompts.
slack.webhookFileNote: An incoming-webhook URL for progress lines (started, PR opened, merged). Mode 600. Without it, no progress posts.
slack.botTokenFileNote: A bot token with chat:write, for asks and the reviewer DM. Mode 600. Without it, asks stay in Linear until a machine that has it sweeps them.

reviewer.name: Sam
reviewer.nameNote: How prompts, notes and ticket comments name the reviewer.
reviewer.githubNote: Their GitHub login. It is requested as reviewer, and its review is the only one that counts for a judgment PR.
reviewer.slackUserNote: Their Slack user ID, for the one DM per PR.
reviewer.fallbackChannelNote: Where the DM goes, with a mention, when Slack refuses it (the app's Messages tab is off).
reviewer.reviewerNote: The human who reviews judgment-path Sentry fixes. The dispatcher requests their GitHub review, comments on the ticket, and DMs them once per PR. Only judgment-path PRs wait on them.

fleet.primaryAccountNote: The account whose config folder is ~/.claude, used by the human's own sessions. The dispatcher spreads work away from it. fleet.sh always labels ~/.claude a, so keep this at "a".
fleet.mainCheckoutWritableDirsNote: Folders under repoPath that fleet/hooks/protect-main-checkout.sh leaves open to file writes, e.g. [".claude/builds"] for a build skill's state. git run from inside them stays blocked. Name only folders the repo's .gitignore ignores. worktreesDir is always open.

dispatcher.enabledHostsNote: Short hostnames (hostname -s) that run ticks. A host not listed does nothing.

hosts.hostsNote: Per machine. maxWorkers is a hard limit on working sessions there: queue workers, engine runs and sessions started outside the queue all count, and nothing automatic starts, respawns or wakes a session past it (a ticket that needs one waits in the wake queue). 0 drains its regular slots; set sentryWorkers to 0 too to drain the machine. accounts limits which fleet accounts it may use; fallbackAccounts get work only when no regular account can take it. maxLoadPerCore and minMemoryFreePercent override the defaults below. sentryWorkers are side slots kept for Sentry tickets. burstWorkers (default 0) are extra regular slots that open while the machine is calm (burstLoadPerCore, burstMinMemoryFreePercent below, which a host entry may override); the Sentry pool and a drained machine get none. platform (optional) is the machine's Node platform (darwin, linux) for platformLabels, when its heartbeat has not said yet. engines (optional) lists the engines that may run on that machine, out of dispatcher.externalBuilders.fallback.engines: absent means every one of them, [] means none.

dispatcher.holdNewWorkNote: true stops this machine from claiming a new ready ticket. To hold every machine at once, run `dispatcher.mjs hold` (it writes <paths.sharedDir>/HOLD; `release` removes it). Unlike a pause, which also stops merges, work already claimed carries on: PRs merge, workers are replaced and woken, and the wake queue drains. Sentry triage queues nothing while held.
dispatcher.burstLoadPerCoreNote: A machine's burst slots (hosts.<name>.burstWorkers) open while its 5-minute load is under this times its cores. null means half of maxLoadPerCore, or 0.75 when that is unset.
dispatcher.burstMinMemoryFreePercentNote: Burst slots also need at least this much memory free. null means twice minMemoryFreePercent, or 40 when that is unset.
dispatcher.wakeRequestHoursNote: A wake override (`dispatcher.mjs wake ENG-123`) that no machine holding the ticket takes within this many hours is dropped. null means 24.
dispatcher.wakeQueueMaxReadFailuresNote: A ticket in the wake queue whose PR cannot be read on this many ticks in a row leaves the queue, so it stops holding a slot, and the human hears once. null means 6.
dispatcher.heartbeatFreshMinutesNote: Another machine's heartbeat counts only when it is younger than this, for the reserve and for status. null means 60.
dispatcher.maxConcurrentNote: Workers across all machines, counted through the building label. A bundle counts as one.
dispatcher.maxDispatchesPerDayNote: null means no daily cap. Worker slots and maxConcurrent still bound the queue.
dispatcher.maxLoadPerCoreNote: A machine whose 5-minute load average is over this times its core count claims nothing that tick.
dispatcher.minMemoryFreePercentNote: A machine with less memory free than this claims nothing that tick (macOS memory pressure level, or MemAvailable on Linux).
dispatcher.headroomFloorPercentNote: An account needs at least this much left in both its 5-hour and weekly windows to get work.
dispatcher.workerCapNote: fleet.sh --max-workers for each dispatch: the working background sessions one account may hold.
dispatcher.workerCapByAccountNote: Per-account caps in place of workerCap, as {"<label>": n}. 0 keeps an account off queue work.
dispatcher.workerReservePercentNote: Percent of an account's week each running worker is assumed to use, by plan (fleet.sh's subscriptionType), e.g. {"max": 4, "team": 8}. An account takes a new worker only while its weekly usage left, less the reserve of its running workers on every machine and the new one, stays at headroomFloorPercent, and accounts are ranked by that figure, so one tick's tickets spread out. Machines share their counts through the heartbeat. {} turns it off.
dispatcher.stallHoursNote: Hours with nothing moving (no commit, no PR activity, worker not busy) before the human gets one stall note. A ticket goes stuck only when its worker has also ended.
dispatcher.spinHoursNote: Hours a worker may stay busy without a commit or PR change before it counts as stalled.
dispatcher.longRunNoticeHoursNote: An informational "still going" Slack line every this many hours of a ticket's build.
dispatcher.stuckInARowTripsNote: This many stuck tickets in a row pause the dispatcher.
dispatcher.maxRedispatchesNote: Replacement workers a ticket gets before it can go stuck: when its worker's session dies (a reboot, say), and when its worker ends on a PR that conflicts with the base branch or holds unresolved review threads (seen on two ticks). The old session is stopped first; a replacement never starts while it could not be. On a full machine the replacement waits in the wake queue; `dispatcher.mjs wake ENG-123` lets one ticket's next wake through over the limit, once.
dispatcher.flakeWaitMinutesNote: How long a failure on a merge commit waits for a later main commit to pass the same workflow before it pauses the queue.
dispatcher.modelNote: The model queue workers run (fleet.sh dispatch --model). "fable" runs Fable while the account may (fableMinWeeklyLeftPercent, fableFloorPercent) and modelFallback once it may not.
dispatcher.modelBySizeNote: A model per Size label for a single ticket, e.g. {"S": "sonnet"}. A bundle and a replacement worker run the regular model.
dispatcher.modelFallbackNote: The model a worker runs when model is "fable" and its account may not run Fable.
dispatcher.fableAccountsNote: Accounts whose workers run Fable while it is allowed, whatever model says. It picks the model only, never the account.
dispatcher.noFableAccountsNote: Accounts whose workers never run Fable. Wins over model and fableAccounts.
dispatcher.fableMinWeeklyLeftPercentNote: A worker may run Fable only while its account has at least this much of its week left (the Fable window aside), so a Fable allowance is spent before the rest of the week.
dispatcher.fableFloorPercentNote: A worker may run Fable only while its account has this much of its Fable allowance left. null means headroomFloorPercent.
dispatcher.burnAccountsNote: Accounts used up first, for usage that would otherwise be lost: one listed here wins every ticket while it has burnFloorPercent left, ahead of the engines and the other accounts, on Fable while allowed unless it is in noFableAccounts. The primary account may be listed.
dispatcher.burnUntilNote: An end to one account's burn, as {"<label>": "<ISO time>"}: from then on it is ranked like any other account.
dispatcher.burnFloorPercentNote: The usage a burn account keeps in both windows before it stops going first.
dispatcher.effortNote: The reasoning effort every queue worker runs at (low, medium, high, xhigh, max).
dispatcher.permissionModeNote: The Claude Code permission mode for queue workers and the red-main responder (fleet.sh dispatch --mode). null keeps fleet.sh's default, bypassPermissions, where a worker can run any command your user can. Run the queue under a user and on a machine where that is acceptable. A stricter mode (auto, acceptEdits) means workers may stop and wait at a prompt.
dispatcher.notifyNote: macOS notifications per transition. Linux hosts rely on Slack.
dispatcher.queueSizesNote: Size labels the queue takes. A ready ticket with another size is sent back.
dispatcher.riskyPathPatternsNote: Matched case-insensitively against every changed path and rename source. A green PR touching one goes to the orchestrator session for review and merge, through the shared merge-requests/.
dispatcher.bundleNote: Up to maxTickets linked agent-ready tickets from one project, each of a size in sizes, share one worker and one PR. A ticket whose description has a 'Ships alone: <reason>' line never bundles.
dispatcher.sentryHeartbeatMinutesNote: While a host with sentryWorkers is unpaused and wrote its heartbeat (sharedDir/heartbeats) less than this many minutes ago, other machines leave Sentry tickets to it.
dispatcher.sentryTriageNote: An optional triage module you write; this repo ships none. It loads from dispatcher/ on host only, when enabled. It exports kickFromTick({ cfg, dry, log }), which should start its run in a detached process, and statusLine(cfg). It labels the tickets it queues with linear.labels.sentry plus mechanical or judgment. A throw or syntax error in it costs one log line and never stops a tick.

fallback.enabledNote: Turns Codex and Grok on as queue accounts on every machine. Off by default.
fallback.enginesNote: Which engines may take tickets. Each machine also needs the CLI installed and signed in, and must pass ext-worker.sh available.
fallback.sizesNote: Size labels an engine may take. Any other size waits for a Claude account.
fallback.maxRoundsNote: Spawns per ticket: the build, then one per fix round. A ticket that needs one more goes stuck, and redispatch hands it to a Claude worker.
fallback.timeoutSecondsNote: The time box of one round. A round that runs over is killed and counts as failed.
fallback.limitCooldownMinutesNote: How long an engine that hit its plan or rate limit sits out account choice on that machine.
fallback.loopbackPortsNote: Loopback ports the sandbox may reach, for local test databases, e.g. [5432, 6379]. Every other local service is refused.
fallback.extraHostsNote: Hosts added to the proxy's allowlist beyond GitHub, registry.npmjs.org and the CLI's own API, e.g. ["pypi.org", "*.pythonhosted.org"]. The engine can send data to each one.
fallback.envNote: Extra environment for the engine's process, e.g. {"CI": "1"}. Names that look like credentials (TOKEN, SECRET, _KEY and the like) are dropped.
fallback.ghTokenFileNote: A GitHub token for the engine, mode 600. Use one that can push branches and open PRs and nothing more. Without the file the engine gets `gh auth token`, your own sign-in.
fallback.claudeOnlyLabelNote: A ticket with this Linear label never goes to an engine. Put it on work that needs access the sandbox withholds.
fallback.withholdPatternsNote: Extra regular expressions that keep a ticket from the engines when its title or description matches, on top of the built-in email, phone and SSN checks.
fallback.preferNote: Engines that take a ticket ahead of every Claude account while they have room, in this order, e.g. ["codex"]. Burn accounts still go first. [] ranks engines with the Claude accounts by usage left.
fallback.creditBackedNote: Engines that keep taking tickets on paid credits once their plan window is spent, e.g. ["codex"]. This spends money: off ([]) by default. Such an engine reads as creditBackedPercent of its week left while its balance, less creditReservePerTicket for each ticket it is building and the new one, stays at creditFloor. An unreadable balance counts as none. Every reading goes to <paths.stateDir>/engine-credits.jsonl.
fallback.creditBackedPercentNote: The weekly usage a credit-backed engine ranks with while it runs on credits.
fallback.creditFloorNote: The credit balance a credit-backed engine keeps untouched. The reserve counts only the tickets this machine is building: machines sharing one account each hold back for their own, so set the floor with the others in mind. Follow-up rounds on a ticket already started are not checked against the floor.
fallback.creditReservePerTicketNote: Credits held back for each ticket a credit-backed engine is building, so running tickets finish.
fallback.codexModelNote: The model Codex queue workers run (codex -m). null uses the model in ~/.codex/config.toml.
fallback.briefNote: Path to your own engine brief template, relative to the repo root. null uses dispatcher/engine-worker-brief.md.

worktreeCleanup.enabledNote: false turns both the teardown at merge and the sweep off.
worktreeCleanup.dryRunNote: true logs what it would do and changes nothing. Set it false to act.
worktreeCleanup.sweepHoursNote: How often each machine sweeps every worktree of repoPath and of each repos entry.
worktreeCleanup.atRiskAskDaysNote: A worktree the sweep keeps because it holds work GitHub lacks is asked about once it has been kept this many days.
worktreeCleanup.trashDirNote: Where orphan folders go. null means the system trash.
worktreeCleanup.reposNote: Other checkouts to sweep, each {"path", "github", "base"}; base defaults to github.baseBranch.
worktreeCleanup.rebuildableIgnoredNote: Ignored files and folders a build, tests or hooks make again. A pattern without a slash matches any part of a path; one with a slash matches that path from the checkout's root. Any other ignored file keeps a worktree, except an unchanged copy of the main checkout's file at the same path. null, an empty list or an invalid one means the built-in list: node_modules, dist, build, out, .turbo, .next, .nuxt, .svelte-kit, .output, coverage, .nyc_output, .cache, .parcel-cache, .vite, .eslintcache, *.tsbuildinfo, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .venv, target, .gradle, .DS_Store.
worktreeCleanup.keepFoldersNote: Folders holding an agent's own work, paths from the checkout's root with a glob only in the last part. One does not keep a checkout: before the checkout is removed or trashed, the folder is copied to keptFoldersDir/<repo>/<worktree>/<date>/ and checked there, and a failed copy keeps the checkout. null means [".claude/notes"].
worktreeCleanup.keptFoldersDirNote: Where keepFolders are copied. null means ~/.cache/forge/kept-notes.
worktreeCleanup.agentWorktreesNote: Worktrees Claude Code's Agent tool makes, which never get a PR: {"pattern", "idleDays"}, a regular expression for the folder name and the days nothing in it may have changed. One goes when it is clean, every commit is on a branch the remote still has, nothing changed for idleDays, and no process or live ticket holds it. One with commits on no remote branch is kept, and the human is asked about it once, by branch; nothing is pushed. "remote" names the remote whose branches count as saved; a repo with no remote of that name turns the rule off, and the sweep logs that once. null means {"pattern": "^agent-[0-9a-f]{8,}$", "idleDays": 7, "remote": "origin"}; {"enabled": false} turns the rule off.
worktreeCleanup.scannersNote: A git process inside a worktree does not hold it when it is read-only (--no-optional-locks with status, rev-parse, rev-list, log, ls-files, merge-base, cat-file, for-each-ref, show-ref, diff or worktree list) and its parent's command line holds one of these strings. null means ["/queue-board/", "/dispatcher.mjs"], the board's and the dispatcher's own scans.
worktreeCleanup.clonesNote: The standalone clones ext-worker.sh makes for Codex and Grok in the worktrees folder. "dry-run" (the default) logs what would happen and counts them by rule, whatever dryRun says; "on" moves one to the trash once its PR merged or closed, it holds no changes, no operation in progress and no ignored file beyond the rebuildable ones, its HEAD is in the PR's head or on origin/<base>, no process is inside, and no live ticket names its branch; "off" leaves them alone.

orphanLabels.heartbeatMinutesNote: How old another machine's heartbeat may be and still count when the orphan label check reads which tickets that machine holds. An older one makes that machine unreadable, and nothing is reported that tick.
orphanLabels.askAfterMinutesNote: How long a ticket labeled agent-building or agent-stuck must read as held by no machine before the human is asked. Never less than heartbeatMinutes plus 30, so a sync stall right after another machine's claim doesn't ask.

dispatcher.orphanLabelsNote: Each tick reports a ticket labeled agent-building or agent-stuck that no enabled machine's state holds, reading other machines only from their heartbeats. Logged once a day, asked about once, no queue label changed.
dispatcher.worktreeCleanupNote: When a ticket's PR merges or closes, the next tick stops its worker, removes its worktree and then its session (claude rm); a session whose worktree can't be told apart is left, and asked about. The sweep moves former worktrees of this repo that git no longer tracks to the trash, and reports any other folder there once. Only worktrees inside the worktrees folder are touched, compared by real path. A worktree goes only when it is clean (untracked files included, nothing in progress; keepFolders are copied out first), holds no ignored file beyond rebuildableIgnored, its PR merged or closed, HEAD is in the PR's head or on origin/<base>, and no live process holds it; anything else is kept, and kept work asks the human (at teardown at once, in the sweep after atRiskAskDays). A checkout whose only changes are deleted tracked files, with its PR merged or closed, is a teardown that stopped partway and is finished. Agent tool worktrees follow agentWorktrees. A ticket live in this machine's state whose PR GitHub shows merged or closed is treated as finished, and the mismatch is logged. Codex and Grok clones follow clones.

codexAutoReset.enabledNote: Spends the Codex account's free rate-limit resets so they are not wasted. Off by default.
codexAutoReset.hostNote: The one machine that spends them, since one Codex account serves every machine. null means the first of enabledHosts.
codexAutoReset.weeklyTriggerPercentNote: A window at this percent used, with its own reset more than minHoursToNaturalReset away, spends a reset.
codexAutoReset.minHoursToNaturalResetNote: A window that resets on its own sooner than this is left to do so.
codexAutoReset.expiringWithinHoursNote: A reset expiring within this many hours is spent once the weekly window is at expiringMinWeeklyPercent.
codexAutoReset.expiringMinWeeklyPercentNote: The weekly usage at which a reset about to expire is worth spending.
codexAutoReset.minHoursBetweenResetsNote: At most one reset in this many hours. Every spend goes to <paths.stateDir>/codex-resets.json.

dispatcher.codexAutoResetNote: dispatcher/codex-reset.mjs: `node codex-reset.mjs` prints what the rules decide now and changes nothing; the tick spends a reset on codexAutoReset.host when they say so.
dispatcher.platformLabelsNote: Linear labels that limit a ticket to machines of one Node platform, e.g. {"needs-mac": "darwin"}. Such a ticket builds only there, never on an engine, never in a bundle with a ticket that needs another platform, and its Sentry fix is left only to a Sentry machine of that platform. A machine whose platform is unknown never matches.
dispatcher.reposNote: Linear project names mapped to other repos the queue builds in: {"<project>": {"github": "org/site", "path": "~/dev/site", "base": "main", "brief": "site-brief.md", "mergeMode": "orchestrator", "mergeReason": "...", "reviewCheck": null, "requiredChecks": [], "ignoreChecks": [], "riskyPathPatterns": null, "reviewGateBlocks": false}}. path defaults to <workspaceCwd>/<repo name>, base to github.baseBranch, brief (relative to dispatcher/) to worker-brief.md. mergeMode "orchestrator" (the default) sends every green PR to the orchestrator; "queue" merges it here on green, without the pre-merge check, which covers repoPath only. requiredChecks or ignoreChecks judge green by the checks, and reviewGateBlocks lets a BLOCKED review gate through. riskyPathPatterns, when set, replaces dispatcher.riskyPathPatterns for that repo's PRs. An invalid pattern in either list is logged, and the queue merges none of that repo's PRs until it is fixed. {"github": null, "why": "..."} names a project with no repo, and a "default": null entry leaves unlisted projects with none; the queue sends those tickets back. The checkout path must be absolute with no "..", its worktrees folder must resolve inside it, and its origin must name exactly the mapped repo; this is checked at the claim, at a replacement and before a teardown. A machine without such a checkout or without the brief leaves the ticket for one that has. Codex and Grok, Sentry merge paths and migration checks cover repoPath only.
dispatcher.externalBuildersNote: Codex and Grok as queue workers (dispatcher/README.md, "Codex and Grok as queue workers"). Every setting is under fallback (enabled, engines, sizes, maxRounds, timeoutSeconds, limitCooldownMinutes, loopbackPorts, extraHosts, env, ghTokenFile, claudeOnlyLabel, withholdPatterns, brief), each with its own Note in the example config. An engine takes a slot in hosts.<name>.maxWorkers like a Claude worker and is ranked with the Claude accounts by weekly usage left. It never takes a Sentry ticket or a claudeOnlyLabel ticket, and its PR always goes to the orchestrator for review and merge. It uses premerge.installCommand for its dependencies and push.gates for its gated push.

merge.modeNote: How merge-approved.sh lands a PR in github.repo: "queue" enqueues it in GitHub's merge queue and waits for it to land (a repo without a queue merges at once), "direct" squash-merges it.
merge.ciHoldNote: In queue mode, hold the merge queue when its two most recent finished runs failed on the same job, until a later run passes that job. A rollup job that fails only because another job did never counts. A fix (github.fixesMainLabel) still goes in, and QUEUE_PROBE_PR=<n> lets one PR in to give the hold a new run to read.
merge.reviewChecksNote: Check names that count as the passed review: one of them must pass on the head, and none may have failed on it. null means [github.reviewCheck]. With both empty no review is required, and every run says so.
merge.reviewSupportChecksNote: Checks that only request or stamp the review, e.g. ["request-review"]. Their failure does not hold a PR once a review check passed.
merge.requiredChecksNote: Checks that must have passed, besides every reported check passing. Use it for a check that may not have reported yet.
merge.ignoreChecksNote: Regex sources for checks left out of the gate entirely, e.g. a preview deploy that fails on forks.
merge.reviewGateBlocksNote: true accepts merge state BLOCKED, for a repo whose branch rule (a code-owner review, say) blocks a PR the gate otherwise passes. Pair it with adminMerge.
merge.adminMergeNote: Merge with gh pr merge --admin, bypassing branch rules. Only for a repo where the gate above is the review you want.
merge.resolvedThreadsNote: Hold a PR that has an unresolved review thread.
merge.reposNote: Other repos merge-approved.sh --repo <owner/name> may merge, each with the keys above. A key an entry leaves out falls back to the top-level value. The pre-merge check, migration order, and the red-main hold apply only to github.repo. Leave it {} if the queue builds one repo.

mergeNote: The gate merge-approved.sh applies to github.repo: not a draft, no approval on file for an older head (running the script on a PR with none is the approval), merge state CLEAN, HAS_HOOKS or UNSTABLE, at least one check reported and every one passing, and the pre-merge check passing against current main. It stops at the first PR that does not pass. A process without CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (a script, CI) skips the driver lock.

push.gatesNote: Commands gated-push.mjs runs in the worktree before pushing, each an argv array. A failing gate fails the push.
push.envNote: Extra environment for the git push itself, e.g. {"SKIP_PREPUSH": "1"} when the gates replace a slow pre-push hook.
push.protectedBranchesNote: Branches gated-push.mjs never pushes to. Before any gate it asks git where the push lands (a dry run) and refuses a protected branch, or a dry run that fails. null means github.baseBranch, main and master.

premerge.installCommandNote: Runs in the scratch worktree before the check. null or [] skips it.
premerge.checkCommandNote: Runs in the scratch worktree after current main is merged into the PR. {base} becomes the main commit the PR's CI ran against, for a check that covers only what changed since.
premerge.errorPatternNote: A failing check counts as a real failure only when its output matches this. Anything else, such as a killed or timed-out run, holds the merge a tick.
premerge.copyFilesNote: Gitignored files the check needs, copied from repoPath into the scratch worktree when it is first made.
premerge.buildOutputRootsNote: Each package under these folders has its dist/ and *.tsbuildinfo cleared before the check, so old output never shadows this tree.
premerge.migrationsNote: Catches two PRs that each pick the same migration prefix, which pass alone and clash once merged. policy "prefix" fails a new file whose prefix the base branch already uses; "filename", for a migrator that applies any unapplied file whatever its prefix, fails only a file name the base branch already has. A green PR whose new migration clashes goes back to its worker to rename it before it merges. null if your migrations have no ordered prefix.
premerge.actionlintNote: When the merged workflows differ from main's, lint both with actionlint (if installed) and fail on findings main does not have. false skips it.

mainWatch.accountsNote: Fleet accounts an emergency responder may run on.
mainWatch.modelNote: The model the emergency responder runs.
mainWatch.maxWorkersNote: fleet.sh --max-workers for the responder. Set high so it starts beyond the regular worker cap.
mainWatch.realertMinutesNote: While main stays red, alert again every this many minutes.
mainWatch.maxRespondersNote: Responders started per red streak. A second starts only after the first has ended.
mainWatch.ignoreJobsNote: CI job names to leave out of the failing-jobs list, such as an aggregate job that only reports the others.

queueBoard.hostNote: The short hostname (hostname -s) of the machine that runs the board. One board covers every queue machine. hourly-check.mjs reads the board on loopback there and by this name elsewhere. null means the machine the script runs on.
queueBoard.portNote: The board's port. The QUEUE_BOARD_PORT environment variable wins over it.
queueBoard.bindNote: Addresses the board listens on. Literal addresses are bound at start. The word "tailscale" binds this machine's Tailscale address (tailscale ip -4) once Tailscale is up, so your other devices on the tailnet can open the board, and after tailscale serve it answers at the machine's HTTPS name too (queue-board/README.md, "Over HTTPS, for a phone"). Never bind the LAN or 0.0.0.0: anyone who can reach the board can type into a worker's session.
queueBoard.sshNote: How the board reaches each other host in dispatcher.enabledHosts: an ssh destination, or an alias from ~/.ssh/config. A host not listed is reached by its own name. Needs key-based login (BatchMode). The board's own host is read directly; an entry for it only builds the copyable ssh attach command for a viewer on another machine.
queueBoard.namesNote: Short names the page shows for each host. A host not listed shows its hostname.
queueBoard.remoteRootNote: Where this repo is checked out on the other hosts. The board runs node <remoteRoot>/queue-board/collect.mjs (and history.mjs, worktrees.mjs, ext-usage.mjs, send.py) there over ssh, and those read that host's own agent-queue.config.json. A path that starts with ~/, or sits under the board machine's home, is taken relative to each host's home. null means the same place as this checkout on the board's host.
queueBoard.repoRootsNote: Folders whose direct child git repos the Worktrees view scans on every host. Include the folder that holds repoPath. Defaults to workspaceCwd.
queueBoard.extUsageNote: Show each host's Codex and Grok plan usage (ext-usage.mjs asks each CLI's read-only billing call once an hour). false turns it off when you have neither CLI.
queueBoard.healthUrlNote: A URL on the environment your base branch deploys to (staging) that answers JSON with a commit field, e.g. "https://api.staging.example.com/health". hourly-check.mjs reports when it serves an older commit than the branch head for over 2 hours. null skips that check.
queueBoard.realmsNote: The realm each host is drawn as in the Middle-earth views: "rivendell" (elves), "shire" (hobbits), "erebor" (dwarves) or "rohan" (Men). Without this key the first four hosts in dispatcher.enabledHosts get Rivendell, the Shire, Erebor and Rohan in that order. A host with no realm, such as a fifth, is drawn as Men under its own name, on Gondor's fields on the map.
queueBoard.spreadRealmsNote: Whether one machine's workers fill realms beyond its own, so one computer still gets the whole map. "auto" turns it on when exactly one host is enabled. true turns it on for any number of hosts: each keeps its own realm, and the unheld realms are dealt round the hosts in order. false keeps each host's workers in its own realm. When on, a worker takes the realm with the fewest live workers when its ticket starts, keeps it for the ticket's life, and takes its name from that realm's pool. Only the two Middle-earth views and the merge cue change.
queueBoard.nicknamesNote: Name pools for the board's workers. A live worker takes the least recently given free name from the first pool that fits: adhoc for a worker started outside the queue, sentry for a Sentry-slot worker, then a pool keyed by its host name, then by its realm, then other for a host with no realm. When a pool runs out, names get a number ("Frodo 2"). Without this key workers show without names.
queueBoard.reviewChecksNote: Optional regex source for checks that belong to the review besides github.reviewCheck, such as a job that runs or re-requests it, e.g. "^(request-review|claude-review\\b)". The board leaves them out of a PR's CI counts. null leaves out only github.reviewCheck.
queueBoard.reviewNotStartedTitlesNote: Regex sources for the titles a failed github.reviewCheck carries when no review has run on the head yet. Such a failure shows as a missing review instead of a failing one. [] counts every failure as failing.
queueBoard.soundFileNote: The sound settings file (mute, volume, per-event switches, music volume). null means <paths.sharedDir>/queue-board/sound.json, so Mute reaches every Mac. A missing file reads as the defaults.
queueBoard.heraldStatusFileNote: Where the herald (herald.mjs) writes its last report, which the board's sound panel shows. null means <paths.stateDir>/queue-board/herald-status.json.
queueBoard.heraldNotifierAppNote: Where install-herald.sh builds the herald's notification app (bundle id dev.agent-queue.herald-notifier). null means <paths.stateDir>/queue-board/Forge Herald.app.
queueBoard.musicDirNote: The folder of MP3s the header player lists and streams in place. The QUEUE_BOARD_MUSIC environment variable wins over it.
queueBoard.weatherNote: The place whose real weather and daylight the map shows, from Open-Meteo's free API (no key). Shape: { "latitude": 40.0, "longitude": -75.0, "timezone": "America/New_York", "place": "Home" }. timezone defaults to the board machine's, place is a label. null means no weather: the scene stays dry and the sky clock uses the board machine's time zone.

learning.outDirNote: Where the sweep keeps reports/, history.json and cache/. null means <paths.stateDir>/learning. Keep it outside the repo.
learning.ciWorkflowFileNote: The workflow file the CI source reads, e.g. "ci.yml". null finds the workflow named github.ciWorkflow through the Actions API.
learning.skipJobsNote: Case-insensitive regexes for CI job names the CI source leaves out: aggregate or watcher jobs that fail only because another job did, and the review check's job, whose findings the review source counts.
learning.reviewBotLoginNote: The GitHub login whose inline PR review comments count as review findings. A finding's first line reads **[Axis]** Severity: RULE-ID text.
learning.reviewRulesGlobNote: Optional glob under repoPath, e.g. "docs/standards/*.md", for markdown tables of review rules (| TST-21 | Rule name |) that name rules in the report. null shows rule IDs only.
learning.correctionsGlobNote: Optional glob for the human's feedback memory files, e.g. "~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/feedback_*.md". Each new or changed file counts as a correction. null turns the source off.
learning.sshNote: Other machines whose dispatcher.log the sweep reads, as {"<short hostname>": "user@host"}, e.g. {"linux-box": "you@linux-box"}. The log is read from the same stateDir under the remote home. The local machine is always read from disk. --no-ssh skips these.

catalog.title: PR body has no machine-read "Fix:" line in ## Regression proof
catalog.why: CI already rejects it, which is where the cost comes from. Shift it left: a pre-push or PR-create check that reads the body before CI runs, or a generated body that always carries the line.

learning.catalogNote: Your own failure types, checked before the built-in ones (typecheck, lint, network flake, Postgres connection terminated, out of memory). match is a regex source run against "<job> <signature>" (flags default to i). enforce lists strings whose presence in an enforcement source counts as enforced there. recommend is a fix-ladder level from 1 to 6. The example is a PR-template line CI requires; replace it with yours, or set [] if you have none.
learning.enforcementSourcesNote: Extra files or folders searched for a type's enforce strings, each with its fix-ladder level. pattern filters a folder's files (default: every file not starting with a dot). learning/README.md lists the sources always searched.
learning.draftStateNote: The workflow state learning/linear.mjs create files a drafted fix ticket in. It never adds the ready label.
